title: Model work health and safety laws adopted (the Commonwealth)
summary: the Commonwealth replaced its own occupational health and safety law with the Work Health and Safety Act 2011, based on the national model laws, so its duties, codes of practice and high-risk work licences largely match those of the other adopting jurisdictions.

instruments.title: Work Health and Safety Act 2011
instruments.provisions: work health and safety duties, regulator powers, high-risk work licences

direction_rationale: Before the model laws each state had its own occupational health and safety Act, regulations and codes. The Productivity Commission's 2010 benchmarking found that differences between them added costs, particularly for businesses operating in several jurisdictions; in 2025 businesses still reported that the remaining lack of harmonisation increases compliance costs for companies operating across borders.

verified.notes: Assent from the Federal Register; section 2 of the Act as made: 'This Act commences on 1 January 2012.' The Commonwealth Act covers Commonwealth workplaces and employers self-insured under Comcare.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 29 October 2026 (tranche 3: laws in regulatory regimes with no register items) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: the Commonwealth moved onto the national model work health and safety laws. Firms operating across the adopting states now meet largely the same duties and codes, which lowers the cost of multi-state safety systems. Victoria never adopted the model laws, and some states vary them, so harmonisation is incomplete.

marks.reason: One set of duties, codes and licences replaces a separate state regime, cutting the cost of running safety systems in several states.
Businesses can expand into other adopting states without learning a different safety law.

assessment.confidence_note: The Productivity Commission documented the costs of the earlier differences; no evaluation of the gains from harmonisation was found.
